First, let's compute the *squared* distance $S(b)$ between the two points. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}S(b) & =((5b+3)-4)^{2}+((b-1)-2)^{2} \\  & =(5b-1)^{2}+(b-3)^{2} \\  & =(25{b}^{2}-10b+1)+({b}^{2}-6b+9) \\  & =26{b}^{2}-16b+10.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want to minimize $S$, we compute the derivative ${S}^{′}(b).$ This gives

$$
{S}^{′}(b)=52b-16.
$$

The stationary points of $S(b)$ are the points where the derivative ${S}^{′}(b)=0.$ Solving this equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(b) & =0 \\ 52b-16 & =0 \\ b & =\frac{4}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(b)=52>0.$

Therefore, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) reaches a minimum when $b=\frac{4}{13}.$
